identity.title: Bifunctional cytochrome P450/ferredoxin is required for fungal phytochrome assembly at mitochondria.

content.abstract: Mitochondria act as dynamic signaling hubs intertwining cellular metabolism and environmental perception in fungi. Here, we elucidate the assembly of the red-light sensing phytochrome (FphA) at the mitochondrial outer membrane in Alternaria alternata. Phytochrome photoconversion strictly relies on biliverdin biosynthesis by heme oxygenases. While mammalian and plant heme oxygenases localize to the endoplasmic reticulum or chloroplasts, the fungal system uniquely repurposes the outer mitochondrial membrane. We demonstrate that the fungal heme oxygenases HoxA and HoxB form a heteromeric complex integrated into the membrane via mitochondrial import machinery components Mim1 and Mim2. At the mitochondrial surface, only HoxA binds directly to FphA. Genomic screening identified Bifunctional Cytochrome P450 Reductase/Ferredoxin A (BcfA) as the essential physiological electron donor. Quantitative kinetics established that BcfA operates as an asymmetric hub, displaying higher affinity for HoxB than HoxA. HoxB functions as a high-affinity kinetic tether locking the donor at the membrane boundary. Consequently, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of bcfA disrupts red-light signalling. Thus, a multi-protein mitochondrial complex evolved in fungi to wire light perception through spatial compartmentalization.
